appraisal_events.evidence: « la plainte heureuse de la respiration jaillissait toujours, légère, tourmentée, inachevée, sans cesse recommençante » ; « un nouveau chant s'embranchait à la phrase interrompue » ; « tant d'états heureux et tendres comprimés par la souffrance ne s'échappaient pas d'elle maintenant » ; « tout ce qu'elle avait à nous dire s'épanchait ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator transfigures the grandmother's death-rattle into inexhaustible song and into a final tender outpouring addressed to the family, lyrically elevating her at the very moment of physical extinction. Although the consoling hypothesis is voiced conditionally ("Qui sait si", "On aurait dit"), the sustained musical and generous imagery is the narrating voice's own and governs the body of the passage.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Au pied du lit, convulsée par tous les souffles de cette agonie, ne pleurant pas mais par moments trempée de larmes, ma mère avait la désolation sans pensée d'un feuillage que cingle la pluie et retourne le vent. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The mother is rendered wholly passive and dispossessed of thought, reduced by simile to wind-lashed foliage; her one question is also answered away by the doctor. This is a distinct, centrally staged collapse of her position beside the grandmother's elevation.

status_effects.explanation: Locally she is raised, not lowered, by her dying: her breathing is heard as happy, inexhaustible song and as the release of all the loving things she had to say to her family.
She loses all standing as an agent in the scene, convulsed and thoughtless with grief at the foot of the bed.

ambiguities: In the mother's line « maman va recommencer à mal respirer », "maman" denotes her own mother, i.e. la grand-mère, not the narrator's mother, contrary to the reference sheet's default assignment of that surface form.

The grandmother's elevation is delivered entirely through hedged, conjectural framings (« Il me semblait », « Qui sait si », « On aurait dit que »), and the father's closing « Mais je croyais qu'elle ne voyait plus » presses against it; a reading in which the narrator marks his own consolation as illusion is available, though the lyric investment is sustained enough to be read as endorsed.
